facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. This burnout is related to losing a client and covering for team members.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October. Not one thing. We lost a big client, half of our team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs. Just never came back after that.

facts.heading: Work schedule disruption
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He stays up late thinking about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I work as a project manager at a logistics company, and I've been completely burnt out since October. I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, and he sleeps about four hours most nights. He wakes up at 3 AM and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours. I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Sleep routine difficulty
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at 3 AM, he has to start shipping schedules and calculate remaining sleep time, which worsens his situation.
facts.evidence: We have to start shipping schedules, the clients, whether I've forgotten something. Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading nights ahead
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights due to his sleep difficulties.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's physical symptoms
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake. He's slower. He gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Role in father's care
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital and leads appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital and leads. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.

facts.heading: Sole caregiver burden
facts.content: Daniel is solely responsible for his father's care because his sister lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My hungry sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for her father falls on me.

facts.heading: Guilt about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for expressing tiredness when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. It feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who is ill.

facts.heading: Withholding information
facts.content: Daniel does not tell anyone about his feelings of tiredness, including his sister Hannah.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone. Not to Hanah either?

facts.heading: GP tests normal
facts.content: Daniel's GP did blood tests which were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is very patient with Daniel. She makes him tea and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire is hurting
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is wearing that hurt.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's wearing that hurt too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking about weekend
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause stress
facts.content: The emails are a barrier for Daniel. He will come back to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price. Can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Stopped running activity
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. His legs feel like lead now.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead.

facts.heading: Lost a part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He felt that running was one time a week when nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was still one time in the week, nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Pearson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Daniel answers emails always
facts.content: Daniel answers every email, even when he is on bed. Claire hates this.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm on bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid they will let him go due to a restructuring this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Relief and guilt about job
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would feel relieved if he were let go but would feel horrible about it.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Inheritable moves apart
facts.content: Daniel moves apart from his third miss a lot, mostly inherited.
facts.evidence: A lot, mostly. Inheritable.

facts.heading: Shaking hand incident
facts.content: Daniel slept in a colleague and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. His hand was shaking and he thought it was a heart attack.
facts.evidence: I slept in a colleague last week, going nothing, and went and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. Hurry was going and my hand was shaking. We thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Frightening experience on train
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening episodes a couple of times. This happened once on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears losing control or ending up in a state of coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it? That I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping?

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habits
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day and has started having one in the evenings.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day and I've started having one in the evenings

facts.heading: Wine use for coping
facts.content: Daniel drinks wine for an hour, but wakes up three times anyway.
facts.evidence: Easy. It works for an hour. I wake up three anyway.

facts.heading: Wine feeling unhelpful
facts.content: Daniel feels the wine is not helping and feels like he is listing things wrong with himself.
facts.evidence: It doesn't feel useful. It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Carrying burdens at night
facts.content: Daniel thinks he carries burdens during the nights.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think.

facts.heading: Grandfather's coping style
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Daniel's reaction to grandfather
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel states he is just very tired.
facts.evidence: I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Belief about being weak
facts.content: Daniel is unsure if he believes he is not weak.
facts.evidence: I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed small change
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try a very small change to fix time in the evening.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small?

facts.heading: Specific plan for change
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying to fix time in the evening when switching off his phone for 20 minutes.
facts.evidence: Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone. Even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for change
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying to do this around half past nine.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after discussing things in session.
facts.evidence: Tired but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Agreed to next session
facts.content: Daniel agreed to have the next session the following week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week?
